title: Why a Plane Door Won't Open Mid-Flight
description:
What happens if someone pulls the door handle at 35,000 feet? Nothing. The cabin is pumped full of air, much thicker than the thin air outside, and that air pushes on every part of the plane, including the door. On most jets the door is a plug: bigger than its frame, so it has to move inward before it can swing out. The air presses it into the frame with about eight tonnes of force, more than a big elephant.

So next time you sit by the exit... relax.

Sources: Patrick Smith, Ask the Pilot, "Open Door Policy"; AirlineRatings, "Can you open an aircraft door mid flight?"; FAA Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (pressurisation). The eight-tonne figure is our estimate from a cabin pressure difference of about 8 psi on a door of about 1.5 square metres.
